pairs.subject: remote-capability-probing
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/system/health.rs:582 The health report marks the hosted Ollama Cloud capability Ok ('free Ollama Cloud models available') when a settings key is merely non-empty, with no request sent and no basis recorded. It sits in the same rows as genuinely probed items (CLI --version, keyring round-trip, temp-table write), so an expired or rejected key reads exactly like proven availability.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/system/health.rs:584 A hosted-platform availability claim rests on configuration only. HealthCheckItem (health.rs:33-44) has only id/label/status/detail/installable/remediation and no basis field, so this inferred row can't be told apart from the endpoint- and process-probed rows beside it.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/system/binary_probe.rs:63 The context's only probes are local process spawns (where/which, --version). Its files have no remote read path that branches on a peer's advertised header (no reqwest or HTTP client).
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/system/binary_probe.rs:73 Probes are local binary version checks, so no remote round trip is being saved. There is no fragment-vs-metadata choice to make here.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/system/health.rs:574 The remote-provider rows read local settings and send no requests, so there's no spending to stop behind a preflight blocker. The relevant gap is the missing basis, not request waste.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject has no rung for local-host capability probes (PATH/--version/keyring round-trip). A context like this one, which mixes local process probes with config-inferred rows about hosted providers, falls between remote-capability-probing, health-checks and optional-dependency-degradation. verdict-basis-tagging could state outright that a 'configuration present' basis is weaker than 'plan' and must never render as an available/Ok status.
